pageCache.pageTitle: Apple Orchard - Therapeutic homes for young people
pageCache.text:
Therapeutic Care with Education
Welcome to Apple Orchard
At Apple Orchard, we provide therapeutic care and education for young people with complex needs. Our homes are designed to support and nurture adolescent males who have faced trauma and exhibited harmful sexual behaviour. Through a tailored approach, we work alongside each young person to promote positive change, build confidence, and guide them toward a better future.
Our highly skilled team uses a variety of therapeutic models, including the Good Lives Model, to create a safe, nurturing environment where young people can heal and thrive. We believe in the power of relationships to drive change, providing a supportive community where every young person’s individual needs are respected.
As part of the Polaris community, we are committed to the very best outcomes for every child and young person in our care. Together, we strive to create lasting positive impacts that empower young people to reach their potential.
Good Lives Model
Strength-based approach, helping young people strive
We use a strength-based approach, focusing on each young person’s unique needs. Central to our work is the “Good Lives Model,” which guides our flexible, tailored therapeutic approach. Our expert therapists ensure that strategies for addressing harmful behaviour are always adapted to each individual’s needs, delivered through genuine, nurturing relationships. This approach aims to empower young people, helping them build positive futures with open, transparent goals in a supportive and caring environment.
Young people say that they feel well supported and are confident that staff understand them well. They describe feeling a sense of belonging at the home and also within the wider organisation.
Ofsted, October 2024
Our Homes
Orchard House
Orchard House serves as the company Head Office and the Management, Education and Therapy Teams are all based there. All enquiries and referrals go through this office.
Oakdene
Oakdene is located between Horsham and Guildford, and has good access to both local amenities and the larger facilities that Guildford and Horsham have to offer.
Fastbridge Farmhouse
Fastbridge is a semi-independent home which has a particular remit to work with young people in ways which will foster increased independence.
Bramley House
Bramley was our first home opening in June 1991, since the early days this home has been radically refurbished and developed to incorporate up to eight young people. It is situated in a small suburb of Guildford, Surrey.
About Us
At Apple Orchard, we provide a nurturing, therapeutic environment where young people aged 12–18 can thrive. We are a specialist residential care and education provider offering a highly structured and supportive setting tailored to meet the complex needs of each individual in our care.
Our School
At Apple Orchard School we believe in creating a culture where the boys within in our care arrive every day with a sense of pride and worth.
Careers
Working at Apple Orchard means joining a compassionate, multidisciplinary team dedicated to nurturing genuine, transformative relationships.

pageCache.text:
Careers
View our current vacancies
At Apple Orchard, we are committed to making a meaningful impact on the lives of adolescent males with complex needs.
Our therapeutic homes provide a supportive, carefully structured environment where young people can heal, grow, and prepare for the next steps in life. We believe every young person deserves a safe, caring space in which to address past traumas and develop healthier patterns for the future.
Working at Apple Orchard means joining a compassionate, multidisciplinary team dedicated to nurturing genuine, transformative relationships. Our Care, Education, and Therapy staff collaborate using evidence-based models such as the Good Lives Model, Family Therapy, Individual and Group Therapy, and our ICON outreach services . Whether you’re an experienced practitioner or just beginning your journey in therapeutic care, you’ll find opportunities to grow professionally and contribute to well‑designed care plans that empower each young person.
Our setting combines the tranquillity of rural Surrey and Sussex locations with close‑by town amenities — ideal for providing both safety and a sense of real‑world community. Orchard House also serves as our headquarters, housing our management, education, and therapy teams, and acting as a hub for assessment and referral.
If you’re eager to make a tangible difference in the lives of young people through high‑quality, therapeutic residential care, Apple Orchard offers an environment where your skills and compassion can truly shine.
Here’s what we offer to our valued team members:
Discounts with over 740 retailers, including:
Become a Residential Support Worker
Up to £32,072.35 per annum (includes sleep in shifts) plus benefits
Our Residential Support Workers are caring, resilient, and dedicated to making a difference in the lives of young people. The role can be demanding and emotionally challenging, as we support boys with complex needs and histories of trauma. But it’s also deeply rewarding, with daily opportunities to build trust, celebrate progress, and be a positive role model.
Working within our therapeutic community, you’ll be guided by our relational and trauma-informed approach, helping each young person feel safe, valued, and supported. Our teams are warm, committed, and work closely with each other to provide consistent, nurturing care.
We have vacancies across our homes in Sussex and Surrey. If you’re patient, empathetic, and ready to be part of a purposeful team, we’d love to hear from you.
Looking for Registered Manager, Deputy Manager, Senior Support Worker Roles or vacancies at our school?
Part of the Polaris Community
As one of the largest providers of children’s services and the very first provider of independent fostering in the UK, our community of services span the length and breadth of the whole of the UK.
We provide an extensive range of children’s services, which have grown and developed over our 30+ year history to ensure we can support children across a wide range of needs. By combining our community’s wide scale of services, as well as our local links, we’re transforming the future of children and children’s services.
The Polaris Community has a united commitment to measure and maximise our social value; defining it as ‘The positive emotional, environmental and economic impact we have on the Polaris community and wider society’. This includes opportunities we offer staff and our children and young people, but also how we work with suppliers, create job and training opportunities and our impact on the environment.
Visit Polaris Website
About Us
At Apple Orchard, we provide a nurturing, therapeutic environment where young people aged 12–18 can thrive. We are a specialist residential care and education provider offering a highly structured and supportive setting tailored to meet the complex needs of each individual in our care.
Our School
At Apple Orchard School we believe in creating a culture where the boys within in our care arrive every day with a sense of pride and worth.
Our Homes
Apple Orchard currently have four homes located in Surrey and Sussex, they are ideally located in rural areas which are close to large towns in order to provide both the seclusion and safety of a countryside location and the amenities of larger towns.

Our Curriculum
Intent
The curriculum at Apple Orchard is designed to be ambitious, inclusive, and responsive to the diverse needs of all young people. It ensures access to formal qualifications and is structured to support academic achievement, personal development, and future readiness. The curriculum is coherently sequenced to promote knowledge retention and cross-curricular connections. At Key Stage 4 and 5, students follow a broad and balanced programme that includes core subjects, vocational options, and enrichment activities. The curriculum is dynamic, allowing flexibility for transient learners and ensuring that every student has the opportunity to succeed regardless of their starting point.
Implementation
Delivery of the curriculum is underpinned by skilled teaching, strong leadership, and clear whole-school priorities. Teachers are supported through targeted CPD, wellbeing initiatives, and opportunities for personal growth. Lessons are designed with subject expertise and pedagogical knowledge, supported by comprehensive schemes of work and assessment frameworks. The curriculum is adaptive and inclusive, with diagnostic tools such as SNAP, PIRA, and PUMA used to personalise learning and track progress. Leadership ensures consistency in feedback, engagement, and curriculum scrutiny, while maintaining high expectations for all learners, especially those with disrupted educational histories.
Impact
Young people at Apple Orchard achieve a wide range of qualifications across academic and vocational subjects. They develop essential skills for employment, further education, and independent living. Students leave with a clear understanding of their future options and increased confidence in their abilities. They demonstrate improved literacy, communication, and self-worth, and are equipped with the knowledge and personal qualities needed to thrive. Cultural awareness and tolerance are fostered through enrichment activities, preparing students to engage positively with society. The curriculum ensures that learners not only meet but often exceed their potential, ready for their next steps in life.

Referrals
For more information about our referral process or to request a referral, please email [email protected] or fill in the form below.
Making a Referral
We welcome enquiries from local authorities seeking placements for young males aged 12–18 who would benefit from a therapeutic residential and educational environment.
We’re happy to have an informal conversation to discuss the needs of the young person and how we may be able to support them. If our provision seems suitable, we’ll ask for supporting documentation so our team can assess the referral in more detail.

All about Apple Orchard
Who we are
Apple Orchard was established over 20 years ago with a clear mission: to provide high-quality, therapeutic residential care and education for young people with complex needs. From our beginnings as a single home, we have grown into a trusted and respected provider supporting boys aged 12–18 across several sites in the South of England.
Throughout our history, we have remained committed to creating safe, stable environments where young people can recover from trauma, re-engage with learning, and move forward with confidence.
Our Approach
At Apple Orchard, we provide a therapeutic environment where young people feel safe, understood, and supported. Our approach is rooted in trauma-informed care and built on strong, trusting relationships. Many of the young people who come to us have experienced significant emotional challenges, often due to early-life trauma, attachment difficulties, or disruption. We don’t just respond to behaviour — we take time to understand each individual’s story and provide the consistent care they need to begin healing and building confidence.
Our dedicated team is trained in a range of evidence-based approaches, including cognitive behavioural strategies, attachment theory, and restorative practice. Every young person has a personalised care and education plan tailored to their needs, helping them to develop emotional regulation, build resilience, and make positive choices. We combine structure with empathy, ensuring each young person has clear boundaries, meaningful routines, and the opportunity to experience success — both in and out of the classroom.
We believe that progress takes time, patience, and the right support. That’s why we focus on long-term, sustainable change, supporting each young person to overcome challenges and develop the skills they need for the future. Through consistent adult support, therapeutic care, and a focus on emotional wellbeing, we help young people move from crisis to stability — and from survival to growth.
Our in-house education provision offers personalised learning that helps young people re-engage with education and reach their potential. We create individual learning plans tailored to each young person’s needs, helping them to achieve academic and vocational qualifications, build self-esteem, and develop practical life skills.
We celebrate progress in all forms – whether it’s academic achievement, improved behaviour, or a new-found confidence in learning.
We aim to equip young people with the tools they need for a successful transition into adulthood. This includes support with emotional wellbeing, social development, independence skills, and planning for the future.
Therapeutic input is woven into daily life through structured sessions, key working, and consistent adult support. Our experienced staff use a range of evidence-based techniques, including cognitive behavioural and attachment-focused approaches, to meet the individual needs of each young person.
We believe relationships are the foundation for change. Our team builds strong, respectful connections with young people, offering encouragement, understanding, and a consistent presence. This helps to create a sense of belonging, stability, and hope for the future.
At Apple Orchard, we don’t just care for young people – we help them rediscover their potential.
Careers at Apple Orchard
Working at Apple Orchard means making a real difference in the lives of young people who need support, stability, and care. We are always looking for dedicated, compassionate individuals who are committed to helping young people overcome challenges and achieve their potential.
Whether you’re an experienced residential care worker, teacher, therapist, or just beginning your career in the sector, we provide a supportive working environment with opportunities for growth, training, and professional development. Our teams are made up of people who are resilient, patient, and passionate about helping others — and we invest in our staff just as we invest in the young people we care for.
If you’re looking for a rewarding role where no two days are the same, and where your work truly matters, we’d love to hear from you. Visit our Careers page to view current vacancies and learn more about what it’s like to be part of the Apple Orchard team.
Part of the Polaris Community
As one of the largest providers of children’s services and the very first provider of independent fostering in the UK, our community of services span the length and breadth of the whole of the UK.
We provide an extensive range of children’s services, which have grown and developed over our 30+ year history to ensure we can support children across a wide range of needs. By combining our community’s wide scale of services, as well as our local links, we’re transforming the future of children and children’s services.
The Polaris Community has a united commitment to measure and maximise our social value; defining it as ‘The positive emotional, environmental and economic impact we have on the Polaris community and wider society’. This includes opportunities we offer staff and our children and young people, but also how we work with suppliers, create job and training opportunities and our impact on the environment.
Visit Polaris Website

Assessment & Therapy
Our service is a specialist therapeutic community designed to support young people with complex needs. Therapy is fully embedded in all aspects of the community, creating a consistent, trauma-informed environment rooted within the Good Lives Framework.
We offer on-site access to a dedicated therapy suite, ensuring that therapeutic support is always within reach. Our team of therapists brings a diverse range of qualifications and extensive experience in working with harmful sexual behaviour, delivering tailored interventions in a safe and supportive space.
Every young person undergoes a comprehensive assessment process, which includes psychometric testing (such as intellectual functioning assessments), as well as thorough risk and needs assessments. Tools like the AIM3 or SAVRY are used when appropriate to ensure interventions are personalised and evidence-based.
Support for Staff Teams
Therapists provide regular training, consultation, and wellbeing support to staff teams across the service. In addition, clinical supervision is offered to both the residential and education teams, ensuring staff are supported in their roles and equipped to maintain a reflective, trauma-informed approach in their work with young people.
Assessing the needs of young people
During their first week, each young person meets with the Head of Therapy to help them settle in and begin building a sense of safety and trust.
Additional Services
At Apple Orchard, we take pride in our holistic approach to care. We recognise that strengthening family relationships is a vital part of a young person’s therapeutic journey.
Good Lives Model
At Apple Orchard we base our approach on the Good Lives Model. The good lives model is an approach which steers away from simply looking at an offending behaviour and how to contain it, but rather plays on the resilience of young people in building better lives.
